utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we have the testimony of the witness, this Trial Chamber would like to deal with some procedural matters. We are seized of a motion for the closed session for the second witness on the list. I would like to know whether there is any objections from the Prosecution side. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the witness number 2 is appointed to me to cross-examine, I would like you to consider one thing. Sometime ago, we had some precedent here in the Defence case already, when the same or identical motion was filed, just to have a closed, completely closed session. It seems to me that that practice proved to be very good, from one point of view we have all the range of protective measures and from the second point of view, we still have a sort of transparent proceedings. So this is our Prosecutor's opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for this specific witness, are you for it or you oppose it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: As for this specific witness, I back up your previous precedent. I think that protective measures such as voice, face distortion and pseudonym would be enough, and at some point we can go into private session without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, as a principle, I believe that all the trials should be conducted in open session, in public session, which is the right of the accused, and it's the job for this Trial Chamber to guarantee that right was not damaged in any way. But in this case, the motion was filed by the Defence counsel and out of an abundance of caution, as well as with the understanding that the motion for the closed session should only be granted in a reasonable and extraordinary circumstances, we grant this motion for the closed session for this witness. But I hope in the future the Defence counsel will take into consideration the right of your client for a public hearing, which means that the motion for the closed session should only be granted in extraordinary circumstances. Yes. Could we have the witness, please? Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Just two things that I would like to inform you with. First of all my client is not here. He is not feeling well. He is not going to attend today's hearing. But he has given me his power of attorney, signed power of attorney to represent him. Another thing. Today at 6.00, all of us counsels have a meeting to finalise the establishment of the bar, of a bar, with this Tribunal, and I believe that we should all attend this meeting, because it is happening after seven years. This meeting is at 6.00, at 1800 hours today. So I could kindly ask the Chamber to give us the grant of leave, because I believe that all of us counsel should be present. So if you agree, I'm kindly asking you if we could finish today at 6.00 as to enable us to attend this very important meeting for all of us Defence counsel. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite familiar with the procedures for this meeting as well as for this bar council. Is it necessary for all the Defence counsel to participate in that meeting? I understand that each team has a lead counsel as well as a co-counsel to represent their clients. Is it necessary for both of you to attend that meeting, whether had involves any vote or something like this? I'm not quite sure. Maybe you could enlighten me, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours. I am not too familiar with the proceedings. The only thing I know is that a list of the Defence counsel's, members of the bar, counsel, will be made. All of us will have to sign the admission form, so in this case, it doesn't really matter whether somebody is counsel or a co-counsel because a list will be put together of all the Defence counsels who represent clients before this Tribunal. This is how I understood the invitation to this meeting today at 6.00. But maybe during the break, we can obtain some additional information and we can shed some more light on what is going on during the meeting, and maybe you can assist us with that. If it is really not important for all of the counsels to be present, then only one of us will go and the other will remain. In any case, I thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course, during the break, I think this Trial Chamber also will make some inquiry about the nature and the procedures of this meeting and later on, we will make a decision on this matter. As you understand, we are a little bit behind schedule because we are planning to have five witnesses this week, but now we only have one, unfinished yet so we have to seize every opportunity to conduct our hearings. But as always, we'll give your motion a favourable consideration. Mr. Seric, before the witness comes into the room would you please brief me on how long you're going to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am hoping to take another 45 minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I am convinced that we will be able to adhere to the schedule of five witnesses this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are very optimistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've been that way all my life, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down. Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can I please ask the usher or the technical booth to lower the ELMO so I can have visual communication with my witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic, did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic, do you know Halil Ajanic, also known as Lopata?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] Another microphone.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What do you know about him specifically? Let me repeat the question, or maybe you can start giving your answer already. The question was: What do you know specifically about Halil Ajanic, also known as Lopata?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- I've known Halil Ajanic, Lopata all my life. And as I've already said, I'm of technical profession and I very often work on various buildings, just like other people in my walk of life, and wherever there is a building site, he will be somewhere near. He always tries to make some money. He is unemployed, and he tries to make money. I know him as a person who drinks, who is an alcoholic, very messy person, sloppy person, a person who has been in treatment for psychiatric disorders on several occasions. But I also know him as a person who is always around, in town. You can see him everywhere, at all times. He's always there. And if not him, then one of the members of his family, because the family had a lot of members.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the incident when his son was killed?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know, I heard on the street from other people, and at the child's burial, at the child's funeral. So I do know some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What do you know?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little, as a matter of fact. His son found a grenade, whether he played with it, whether the bomb -- there was something wrong with the grenade, I don't know, but I know that he got killed. It was a very sad story, but I think that Halil had six or seven children, I don't want to be wrong on that, and I know that he could barely feed them, let alone bury them, and then we raised some funds to help him bury that child who had gotten killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know where this happened, where did this explosion take place, in which this boy got killed?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I believe it was close to the base, in a private house, or in an apartment inhabited by this soldier. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was using this apartment?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean who was in the apartment, I can tell you that it was a soldier, a foreigner, a German national, I believe. I'm not sure of that but I know that he was a foreigner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the relationship between Vinko Martinovic and Halil Ajanic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no particular relationship to talk about, but he always had a better relationship with those who would give him some work to do, who would give him some money, a few coins. Halil was always around. He was always to be seen. Halil was Halil. And that's the long and short of it. He was just a joker, and he was always there. He was always around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he perform any works during the war, either for Vinko or for you?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I have understood you well. Halil could not perform any works. He did not have any tools to perform works with. He could load things, unload things. He could clean things on the condition that he was sober. He was always around. I don't exclude the possibility that he may have done something. He was always, when he was around we would call him to give us a hand and we would give him some small change in return.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Halil Ajanic was brought as a detainee into the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Would you be familiar with the reason for which Halil Ajanic would testify against your brother, Vinko?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that's a question too far. I think that counsel's properly asked background facts upon which arguments can be made but I think this to ask him to state the opinion of what's in Mr. Ajanic's mind is too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's kind of speculation. Maybe you could rephrase your question in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any circumstance or any event which would instigate Halil Ajanic to testify in this case on the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Only if he bears a grudge, if he did not help him enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were you, Mr. Martinovic, personally, on the 17th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you not recall that date?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date as a date, it must have happened, but I don't know where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: If I remind you that on that date, there was a large-scale conflict in Mostar between the BH Army - we are talking about September, 1993 - between the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the one side and the Croatian Defence Council on the other side, would you be able to remember?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were you at the time? Did you participate in the war operations?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not know the date, but I was in Mostar on that day. It was a day like any other in Mostar, but there was a lot of -- a lot more shooting. Let me put it this way: It was a lot noisier than on any other day. So it was a real war. And nothing else was going on in the city. There were more ambulance vehicles and it was a lot more noise. There was a lot more of those things which happened during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were you on that particular day? In town?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you in any way involved in any of the actions?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Vinko was on that day?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course; he was on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about the fact that, in that operation, war detainees, prisoners of war, were used as human shields on any section of that front line?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the allegation in the indictment, and you did say that you had an opportunity to read it, in the papers, that on that particular day, on the 17th of September, 1993, in the Vinko Skrobo unit, prisoners of war were used as human shields alongside a tank and that they were given wooden rifles for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a point of clarification. It's not clear to me, and I don't know, perhaps the counsel's satisfied with the answer, I'm not sure, but there have been several questions and answers over the last few minutes and the last one, I'm sorry, I can't seem to get the -- the question at line ten was, "Do you have any personal knowledge about the fact that in that operation, war detainees, prisoners of war, were used as human shields on any section of that front line?" The answer is, "No," so I assume the answer means he has no personal knowledge one way or the another other. He has no knowledge about the event at all. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Seric, would you please make some clarification by asking a question to this witness? Because "No" could be interpreted in two ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Your answer, when you said "No" to my question, could mean either that you do not have any knowledge or it can also mean that prisoners of war were not used as human shields. Can you please clarify the meaning of your negative answer.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you now asking me about the date of the 17th of September, or generally?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: The question is relative to that particular date. So mid-September, 1993, or more specifically, the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer, I would like to say to this Trial Chamber, although it may sound a bit -- this was a day with a lot more shooting than usual. I don't know whether it started in the morning or in the afternoon, but it went on throughout the day. Somebody was playing war games but the day was not so much different than any other days, to my mind. Maybe it was different for the fighters on the front line. I don't know if anything special was happening on the front line. I don't know. And the answer to your question whether people were used as human shields, the answer is no, and I don't have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I will go back now to my other question. Have you been informed about the allegation in the indictment that that day, prisoners were used as human shields and that they were given wooden rifles? And did that happen precisely in the unit under your brother's command?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of that. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what really happened that day, the 17th of September, 1993, on the front line, in front of the health centre?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk with Vinko Martinovic about those wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour my objection again. Let me object again to the nature of this particular testimony and let me amplify what I said yesterday. Your Honour, it would only be too easy for any accused in this case to speak to a friend or relative and give him all sorts of information on which that witness would then come and testify. I think that's improper. We object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, I think yesterday we already ruled on this issue. To this witness, we only want to hear what he personally saw and experienced during that time. And you understand that this witness has a special relationship with your accused. So it seems to us there is no evidential value if the witness tells what his brother told him about this matter. I mean, this witness came here as a witness. He could tell us what his personal experience is, but not what the accused told him, because we put very little weight on this kind of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I realise that, Your Honours, but I also realise that the accused would find himself in the same situation if he were to testify in this Court but I will withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation for the reason to attribute this incident to Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it is a sound explanation but I do have one. When this indictment was published --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, the witness has already said now at least twice he has no knowledge of these events at all, at all. I think this inquiry is over. We object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but the question is that, "Do you have any explanations for the reason to attribute this incident to Vinko Martinovic." That's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour what basis can there be for any explanation on matters on which this witness has said he has no personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this witness lived there. He has his own perspectives on certain matters. We would like to hear the explanation from this witness, whatever it may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask, then, that before the answer be given that the foundation for the explanation be explained. Is it again based on what his brother told him? We are right back to where we were. So if the if he's going to be allowed to give an explanation, Your Honour, the Prosecution ask respectfully that he first indicate the foundation for basis on which that explanation is based.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you may tell us what is your opinion on this issue, not any information told by your brother.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I understand that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me try to meet the requests of the Defence and the Chamber. The answer that we expect to hear from the witness, may I ask the witness a couple of leading questions in order to steer him in the proper direction to give us this explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, I think you asked the question and the witness is ready to answer it. Let's hear the witness first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but Mr. Seric did not say leading question. He said "questions to lay the foundation." Mr. Seric did not say, "A couple of leading questions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would never say that. But never mind, let the witness say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And I'm sorry for the speed with which ideas are exchanged here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After all this, I think I'm the most confused of all. So when this indictment became public, when one could read it in all the press and see it on television, those wooden rifles drew most of attention of all because that was something strange, something out of the ordinary, for many reasons, and I apologise to the Court, but every person that I talked about it with and then the Tribunal was being called something which lacks seriousness, which really lacks sufficient gravity. If anything like that could be put in the indictment. All the more so, as a few months ago, and I cannot say exactly but the Court can find did in the press or somewhere because at that time a similar or identical incident was already being mentioned as something that had happened in the war between the Serbs and the Muslims. So that this is discussed, this has become a pet topic, but which has rather bad ring to it, and which could play a wrong part in the indictment, in the accusations against Vinko Martinovic or somebody else. So that is what I -- why I think it happened and why that became part of the indictment. But I think that this is just something which is not of good quality, something which is semi-manufacture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge why would Vinko Martinovic be sacrificed and surrendered to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about the sequence of events and it is up to you then to decide whether I'm making guesses or whether this is specific knowledge. His Honour is right, he is my brother, and perhaps -- but all these stories, all these gossip, all these tales, now we know everything about Vinko Martinovic more or less, and conditionally speaking he has no pedigree, I mean military or political and he became a target for the press in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia and I mean the press. The front pages, second pages, and so on and so forth. He and his unit, and at some point, a wave of arrests started in the town of Mostar. Before that, something happened that I believe you are all aware of, and that was the -- an attempt against Mr. Hans Koschnik, High Representative of the European Union in Mostar, in the Ero Hotel in Mostar where his residence and his office were. So that day some unpleasant things happened. There were stoning, some vehicles were set on fire. And there was an attempt against Mr. Koschnik. And they came to me to ask me where my brother was. "Why do you want him?" They said they had located him -- they had identified him as the man who organised the attack on Mr. Koschnik. That is what they said. Vinko was in Split that day. Vinko had gone there to visit his wife, who was in the hospital, because she miscarried. So I used my cell phone to call Vinko and this gentleman who came to my place to look for him, I gave -- I handed over the phone so that he could talk with him personally. And of course, he was pretty embarrassed. So they started saying to me things like apologise, sorry, we didn't know, sorry, mistake. If, that is one can call it a mistake, to call him the organiser of the attack on Mr. Hans Koschnik, and he wasn't in the town of Mostar at all. 2.500 men and Vinko Martinovic is presumably their leader. After Mr. Koschnik was succeeded by another High Representative and the first thing he did, he invited Vinko Martinovic for an interview, to tell him that he would not tolerate any organised attacks on him and his team. And Vinko, being the man that he is, says, "I have nothing to tell you about this, because I'm not the man." However, it is a nice and clear example of how a particular situation can be created and how the accusations are directed at one man. And the same time, in a part of Mostar police, arrests are started of people who were in the war, that is Vinko, and I'm giving you firsthand knowledge. In the morning, at half past 4.00, a friend came to wake me up and tell me that the evening before that, four of Vinko's friends had been arrested, that they had been beaten in the prison all night long, and could I do anything, could I go there? Because otherwise, they would be beaten to death if that went on. I waited for 7.00 in the morning to strike. Then I went to the Mostar police, where I was told that that was not true, and that they were not there. After checking with a friend who had informed me originally, whether they had indeed been taken in, I then went to the mayor of Mostar, because I had nobody else to go, Ivan Prskalo, and I asked him to check what was going on. And as he was checking what was going on, he then provided me with some incoherent answer, but meanwhile my friends brought a doctor called Meskic, a Muslim, who at that night was -- went to the prison to attend those beaten. After that, I went to the HDZ Presidency in Mostar, and for me, that was the supreme authority at the time. And asked that the necessary measures be taken, that people -- so that people wouldn't be taken in and beaten for reasons known only to them. Now, I wish to emphasise, in particular, after I was admitted, one hour and a half after that, a meeting was held of, I don't know whether a narrow body or a broad body of that party, and there was a major quarrel there, because obviously half of the people knew what was going on and the other half didn't. Four days later, the first person was set free, released from prison, beaten up, of course, scared, he dared not even tell me good morning, let alone what had happened there. 12 days later, another person was released, darker than this microphone, that is black and blue all over, who said that the interrogation had only, and one subject only, and that was Vinko Martinovic. Paper on the table, write down all that you know about Vinko Martinovic. A month later, a third person came out, but as it all went on, other people were being taken away for a day, two or three, and this whole circus lasted for months. None of the charges have -- not been filed against any one of those people, known of them have been sentenced, none of them are in prison. However, none of them has a passport and not one of them was ever given the explanation for his detention. And they all had one and the same question: Vinko Martinovic, Stela, as they referred to him, as his pet name. So it all tells me that there was some major play involved concerning Vinko Martinovic and I claim that Vinko Martinovic was a matter of a trade between Zagreb and the International Tribunal, or at least such an attempt was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was Vinko Martinovic different from other soldiers in the HVO? And commanders of other units of the same rank?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, physically, of course, yes. As for his possibilities to do something, no. However, there was a huge difference. There was a huge difference. He would not suffer lies. He would not suffer insincerity and it was the kind of his attitude that made him different from others. And as for his command responsibility, I guess if he had any, where he was, I think that it was just as anybody else's neither bigger nor smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And finally Mr. Martinovic s there anything that you would like to add, something that I perhaps have forgotten to ask you and that you would like the Court to know?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, when I defend, when I talk about my brother, then my time is more than short, and I suppose when the Prosecutor comes, then it will look too long, but there is one thing I wish to say. If I've understood correctly His Honour, my testimony does not have much probative value because I'm a brother and I can understand that. However, I wish to say the following and I hope it will not be forgotten, if possible. Vinko Martinovic, for the duration of the war, had never any political or any other support for a single day for a single minute. Vinko Martinovic joined the war, the first one and the second one, out of his conviction, not for, mathematical reasons. Do not let Vinko Martinovic pay for mathematics, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have concluded my direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the other witness's microphone be switched on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in connection with some of your answers just this afternoon, I'll start with those, then go back to yesterday, this child of Mr. Ajanic, who was killed with a hand grenade, as part of all the things you heard, sir, did you did you ever hear that it was one of your brother's men who pulled the pin of this hand grenade and tossed or rolled it to this child as if it was a toy?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You never heard that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In connection with the attack on the life of Hans Koschnik, the international representative in Mostar at the time, can you give the Chamber -- I don't think during any of that, you gave the Chamber a date. Can you tell the Chamber approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that, but this incident did happen, and the date, I can't tell you. That is really my weak point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, surely you can give us some estimation. It wasn't in 1993, was it?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late that year, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Late 1993? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not my testimony. I'm not claiming it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, can you give us your best idea of the event when Mr. Koschnik was attacked?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The witness says he's not getting interpretation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we have to check the channels. Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Scott, would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, give us the best estimate of the date of the attack on Mr. Koschnik that you can?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, then to say, sir, as you said a moment ago, that you have a poor memory of dates?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all, not all dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us please, who was it that you said apologised to you about the allegation that your brother had organised the attack on Mr. Koschnik?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please do. Please give us the name of the person who apologised to you.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An official of the security service called SIS, at least that is what it was called then. His name is Franjo Primorac, and he supposedly got that information in his agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So just so the record is clear, it was no representative or member of the international community who apologised to you, but it was a member of the Bosnian Croat secret police who told you, supposedly that they apologised, that someone apologised to you?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Had you ever had any other dealings with the Bosnian Croat secret police or intelligence service, SIS, apart from that one occasion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you mean by dealings?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have you ever had any meetings or discussions with anyone from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Bosnian Croat intelligence service, apart from this one occasion that you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean about my brother?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: About anything, sir. I'm just asking you, you said this man, the leader of the Croat intelligence service, Mr. Franjo Primorac came to you, you say, and apologised to you about allegations made about your brother. My question to you, sir, is did you have -- have you ever had any other dealings with the Bosnian Croat intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're misinterpreting it. He first affirmed that Vinko Martinovic was one of the organisers and when we established that he was not in Mostar, then he apologised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. My question to you, sir, if you listen to my question, please, had you, other than that occasion, have you ever been had any other dealings with the Bosnian Croat [RealTime transcript read in error "Bosnian Croat service"] intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You have not had -- your answer then, includes that you've not had any contact with any such intelligence service in connection with the Defence of your brother against the charges here?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm following the transcript and I'm listening to the questions, and the question in English and I see the transcript it says, "Bosnian Croat service." I'd really like to know what is that Bosnian Croat service. Could our learned friend be so kind as to explain it to us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if the witness and the Prosecutor both know what it means, I don't think that it's necessary to explain it. I don't think in this case, that the Prosecution is misleading the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, just so I make sure because of the questions raised now and possible of possible language differences, let me make sure I understand your testimony now. To the very best of your knowledge, sir, you're telling the Chamber that no representative or agent or operative of the -- of any Bosnian Croat secret police or intelligence service has been involved in assisting your brother's defence against the charges here?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, please, you say yourself, service. It has a prefix in front of that name. It's secret service. And this is not my environment. This is not my milieu. In the preparation of the defence of my brother, I believe that a lot of people have been involved. Were any of them from the service or not, please don't ask me. I believe that your question is hypothetical. I do not know that I have spoken to, that I have been involved in the preparations of the defence of my brother with anybody who is a member of any secret service, and I believe that with that, I have made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So to the extent you might have talked to such a person, you didn't realise that you were talking to such a person at the time, is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, the four people that you said were arrested, can you again give us some time frame? In direct examination, sir, absolutely no date or time frame was given for this event. Can you please tell us when it was that these allegedly, four friends of your brother, were arrested?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can't give you the date, as I've already said, but they were arrested, not only the four of them, the first four of them were arrested during the first night and the later on, there were 12 more of them who were brought in for interrogation, and it was precisely during the period when Vinko Martinovic was in custody in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So can you give us an approximate date, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give us the names, please, of these four people who you say were arrested at this time, for which we don't have a date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Just for precaution, because of these people who are possible witnesses, I would like us to go into private session, if we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you said that in connection with this event, you went eventually, you went to the HDZ Presidency about this matter. Can you once again please, give me the name of the individual, official or persons that you approached about that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. At the reception, I was met by a person who asked me when I was born, why I was born [as interpreted], and then referred me to another person, one floor up. The same was repeated there. And then I asked to have a word with the President, because that was the last instance that I could contact, but I at that time had a feeling that this was the highest level where I can raise my complaint. And I spoke to Mr. Bozo Raic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Bozo Raic. And what time period was this that he was the mayor of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that he was the mayor of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My mistake, you're absolutely correct, sir. When was he the president of the HDZ political party?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in 1993 and 1994, but I can't claim that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, now, sir, in answers to direct examination, if I heard you correctly, you said that at the time you considered the president of the HDZ to be the supreme -- you testified, sir, that you considered the president of the HDZ to be the supreme authority in Mostar. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I assumed at the time that it was the supreme authority that -- who was in the position to check whether the information that I had received was correct or not, whether the thing that I heard about really happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, why did you consider the president of a political party, the HDZ, to be the supreme authority over the mayor or elected officials of the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you are talking from an office, and you know the situation in the city, from a letter that somebody sent to you. The situation was not such as to be -- for one to be able to say that the order was respected, and there was no real hierarchy of instances, so if the situation had been normal, I would have received the accurate information already in the police station. When I didn't receive it in the police station, I turned to the mayor, who told me, "I'll see what I can do." I did not have the time to spare for him to see what he can do. I went elsewhere. I went and turned to another level. And that's the long and short of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the clock and I'm about to change topics, if it would be a convenient time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 4.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before you start, Mr. Scott, we have made an inquiry during the break to the Registrar about the meeting for the Defence counsel. We were told that this meeting was organised by the Defence counsel, not by the Registrar. So since we are behind schedule, we will continue to sit after 6.00 but any co-counsel of the Defence team to like to attend the meeting, they are free to go. It is so decided. Mr. Scott, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have the usher's assistance, I'm going to ask that a clean copy of Exhibit P11.18 be placed before the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No translation? No interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear you. I don't have interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can. MR.SCOTT: Mr. President, let me inquire of both you and through you to counsel, I'm going to ask some questions of the witness about some locations in connection with the Martinovic family and I don't know if the Defence considers that to be protected or sensitive information or not. So I will inquire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric? Mr. Seric? Can you hear me? Do you need the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it would be wise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I may have misspoke or you may have misheard me, but I was asking what commerce your brother was engaged in and at least in the translation you came across, you referred to a "she." What commerce was your brother Stela engaged in during that time?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What I am saying, he was selling haberdashery and miscellaneous wares for households and children's toys.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that your brother had a number of what some of us might call run-ins with the legal authorities during those years?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during those years. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sometime, then, when did he have the problems with the law enforcement authorities in the Mostar region?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While he was under age, that is before he turned 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, given that answer, in terms of the age of the accused, I won't pursue it further at this time, although frankly, I think that given the practice in the Tribunal, this would be relevant for a number of reasons, including sentencing, if we should get to that point, and as you may know, Mr. President, there is no separation of the guilt and innocence phase, if you will, and the sentencing phase of these proceedings but nonetheless, I will not go further into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did your brother join HOS?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose the same day when the Yugoslav People's Army came to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, I suppose you can't give us any time frame for that? Or can you?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, no matter how many historians or people who survived the war in Mostar, you ask about when the Yugoslav People's Army came there, some will tell you it was on the 21st, others will tell you that on the 13th that they were on hill slopes. When did it arrive? I'm sure you have somewhere -- you have it somewhere written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, so then we will just take it, sir, your testimony is that on the first day, whenever that happened, on the first day of that, your brother joined HOS? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I believe you said that he joined HOS at a village near Mostar, and I was just curious what village that was, please.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a camp, a training camp, or something like it, a place where those young men gathered. It was outside the town. That camp was or that place, whatever you like, you can call it whatever you like, it was in a field called Mostarsko Blato and its boundaries, there are three villages along its boundaries. One is called Ljuti Dolac, the other is called Biograci and the third one is called Jare. Now, which village it belonged to, there are -- all these villages are in a string, once they were separated, but you can call it one village and you can call it whatever you like, and I'll certify that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I believe you testified, as is it correct, that your brother became the commander of the HOS in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did he continue to be the commander of the HOS Mostar throughout the existence of that unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you were asked questions about when that unit dissolved or ceased to exist and again I suppose you don't know the approximate time when that happened, or do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It fell apart after the conflict, after the war ended, between -- with the Serbs, that is after the Serbs left the positions in and around Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did the HOS unit dissolve or disband, was this after the leader of HOS in Herzegovina, Blaz Kraljevic, was murdered?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that ultimately your brother took most of the people who had been the members of the HOS in Mostar and joined the HVO? Perhaps not immediately, but that's ultimately what happened, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like the usher to show you, please, what's been marked as Exhibit 876.051. It should be in the bundle of exhibits that have been distributed for this witness. There is a Croatian language version attached, sir, if you can find your way to that, or the usher can assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention, sir, if you can find in your version there is a section which lists it four commanders and you may be able to find it if you look for a numbered section, a list of other people --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, this is a new document. This is an alleged expert analysis done by some generals of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is called a new document and again it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. says, "BH government." Your Honours, such an exhibit, whose origin we do not know, we do not know who wrote it, it was evidently written at the request of the gentleman in the Prosecution, I do not think that such evidence can be of any use in this Court because these experts should have come here and testified. And therefore support their analysis, and make cross-examination possible, if that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this witness is not your witness. It's Mr. Seric's witness, and we have come across this issue for many times already. We will let the Prosecution proceed with his question, and later on, we will decide on the admissibility of this document. We will take into consideration your objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours, but let me tell you exactly it is -- they are indeed witnesses for my colleague but I'm not isolated here, because I see that identical documents are produced here and those which were shown my witnesses, if I can call them my witnesses, because I think that they are all witnesses of the Court rather than Mr. Seric's or my witnesses, or Prosecutor's witnesses. But it doesn't really matter how we call them, here in the parlance of this courtroom, I cannot be isolated in my objections, regardless of which witness we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have already said that we will take into consideration your objections concerning this document when we are admitting those documents into evidence. Let us hear the question from the Prosecution first. And I also believe that the witness has the full right to agree or disagree with the contents of this document. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I go back, return to my question, sir, let me just -- you testified on direct examination, is it correct, sir, that you also were a member of HOS, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I know we have problems with dates but, sir, the Chamber needs to have some idea of when these events occurred. From approximately when to approximately when were you a member of HOS?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd say June, 1992, end of 1992, to make it easier for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, I was going to come back to this later, sir, but didn't you testify on direct examination that in fact when you were moving around Mostar, on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, that you were still a member of HOS?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the date, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time that you told the Judges that you were moving about in Mostar, on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, did you not testify that you were still a member of HOS at that time?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I perhaps misspoke, but absolutely not, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Returning to the exhibit in front of you, which for the record again is 876.051, if you could find the portion where you'll see a list of four numbered names, in the Croatian version, the list your brother Vinko Martinovic, Stela, as one of the commanders in Mostar, correct? In the Mostar region?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as you've told us already, that's accurate, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other three individuals, Mr. -- The two Mr. Batlaks and the fourth individual?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under number 4, I am familiar with that last name Sisirak, and I believe I knew him. The other two, Batlak, is a very common last name in Mostar so I cannot be any more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You will move to the section that's under the heading -- you'll find the heading that says, "The HOS in Herzegovina." You see a section that describes and I'm looking, Mr. President, for the English readers on page 2 of the translation, about the middle of the page -- indicating that the commander of HOS, Blaz Kraljevic was posted at the HOS headquarters in Ljubuski. Now, did you know that to be correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Had you ever met or had any dealings with Mr. Kraljevic prior to the time he was murdered?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in the HOS headquarters in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that Blaz Kraljevic was murdered because of conflicts between the HDZ and the HOS?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that. HOS was a military formation, and the HDZ a political party, so that I don't see any link.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, during the time that you lived in Mostar, during these years, and in that region, did you ever -- did you understand that HOS was a unit that -- an organisation that believed more in a multi-ethnic Bosnia of the Croats and Muslims working together? Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I thought too. It's not that I heard it. I thought so too, and that's what HOS was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And wasn't it because of the HDZ's conflict with that philosophy, that Mr. Kraljevic was ultimately murdered?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but I am not the person who can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm trying to look, sir, if I can assist you in giving you a reference point so that's why I'm pausing. Sir, it says in the document, and I cannot find it offhand, the Croatian language version is only two pages, so you can perhaps find it, but on page 4 of the English version, it says that the Mostar HOS, led by Vinko Martinovic, aka Stela, went over to the HVO. And that is ultimately correct, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your brother never joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, that was my question, sir. After your brother left HOS, he did in fact join, whether it was the next day or sometime later, he joined the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I read here nicely in this expert opinion, which was written by four Muslims, that the HOS unit, after it was disbanded, was attached to the Croat Defence Council, but this same document also says that 70 per cent of this unit was made up of soldiers who were of Muslim origin. Now, if I said yesterday that Vinko lined up his soldiers and said, "Well, each one pick up his rifle and go wherever he wants to," because it was obvious that there could be a conflict within the unit, then one can assume who went where. Nevertheless, your experts say that Muslims went to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what Vinko did, he did. Who went where, I cannot know. You allow me to finish. So what Vinko did was to dissolve his troops, and I said it yesterday, I wasn't happy to say that in front of him and I said how that was inglorious and everybody went where he thought he belonged to at that particular moment. Yes, you may go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, thank you, sir. I appreciate that. Sir, these are not my experts, so just to correct you about that. It has nothing to do -- the document was not produced for the Office of the Prosecutor, contrary to counsel's representations. But my question to you, sir, was only this: Sometime after your brother left HOS, where he was the commander of the Mostar group, he joined the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to that, then. By approximately, if I heard you correctly, sir, by approximately the end of May or early June, 1993, your brother Stela had formed this unit called Mrmak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the HOS unit was dissolved, Vinko Martinovic went home, literally home. In the true sense of the word, he went home. And he began to work for a car wash. He had civilian clothes on. That unit that you asked me about, and which is called Mrmak, was formed not long after the beginning of the conflict with the Muslims, and do not ask me the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So I was --

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, believe me, I do not know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we understand that at this point. My answer -- my question to you then, sir, it was correct to say that sometime in a few -- a short time after the attack on Mostar on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, whether that was two weeks later, three weeks later, sometime after that, your brother formed the unit Mrmak, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps he called it that. He named it that. But I presume that the unit was formed by somebody who commanded at the front line, somebody who planned that -- who planned the defence of the city of Mostar, but it is a fact that he led that unit and was at its head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it was that same unit, sir, that later became the Vinko Skrobo unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've told the Chamber many things about your brother, sir. Is it your testimony to this Chamber that your brother is a person who speaks the truth?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it your testimony to this Chamber that your brother is a person who speaks the truth?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally or in a specific instance?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Generally, sir.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he is a person who speaks the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like the usher to please show you Exhibit P633, which the English version could be placed on the ELMO, please? Sir, I'll ask to you look at the Croatian language version and I'm going to direct your attention to the section immediately under the section titled "record of interrogation". And I'll simply very slowly read that paragraph and I'll ask you a couple of questions about it, sir. "On the 9th of October, 1993, Vinko Martinovic, known as Stela, son of Ivan, born on 21 September, 1963 in Mostar, residing in this address, street number 21, a driver by occupation, married Mirjana -- forgive me if I miss pronounce this, but Jakovljevic, my apology. No children, member of the Convicts Battalion ATG, with a rank of colonel and commander of the Vinko Skrobo ATG unit." Now, sir, can you tell the Chamber, please, is all that information that I've just read to you, as far as you know, is that all true and accurate information?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read to you what I'm sure is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vinko Martinovic is correct. It is correct that he is called Stela. It is correct that he is the son of Ivan and the date of his birth is correct. I know it. The address is correct because this is the address of our family home. The name and last name of his wife are correct. As for the rest, I cannot confirm that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, can you give the Chamber any reason to believe that your brother, who you said a moment ago generally tells the truth, why he would -- is there any reason to believe that he wasn't speaking accurately in giving the other information contained in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that he was not telling the truth. What I was -- what I said was that I can't confirm that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the question because in the question, the Prosecutor claims something that it is not true. This is not Vinko Martinovic's statement, what it says here in the first paragraph. So my learned friend, let me use this term "incorrectly" represents this by saying that this is Vinko Martinovic's statement. How the data were taken remains to be discussed. This is not an integral part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, reading from this paragraph, we saw the last few words, that is made the following statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the later parts are the statement made by Vinko Martinovic. As for the first part, we also have some doubts whether this is the words of Mr. Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Mr. President, let me ask some follow-up questions, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing your attention, Witness, to the -- bottom left corner of the Croatian version. You see a signature or a signature, some handwritten words, under the typed name "Vinko Martinovic"?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that your brother's signature?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but I can't be sure. I wouldn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does it look like your brother's signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does look like my brother's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, looking at the body -- that part of the document, I'll skip over the other part for a moment, perhaps we will come back to it later, but that part under the heading, "Statement," do you have any reason to believe that your brother was not telling the truth at the time he made the statement?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the Prosecutor is using this document and if we have a witness who is asked to talk about this document, why don't we allow the witness to read this entire document first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The witness could read that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The complete document? Okay. "Statement."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't have to read it aloud. Just read it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe, sir, that your brother wasn't speaking truthfully when he made this statement over a signature that looks like his signature, on about the 11th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, as I have already told you, in this record of interrogation, I can say that the names and the last names are correct. The dates are correct. But I can't say that the names of the units are correct, and I do not have any reason to believe that my brother lied or that he had any reason whatsoever to lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge at the time, or around this time, of the event that's described in the text of this report or statement?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not any personal knowledge. I just heard stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, during, about this time, after the Mrmak unit was formed and including the time that it later became the Vinko Skrobo unit, who did you understand your brother's principal deputies or assistants to be? That is what other commanders of units did he have under him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you who portrayed themselves as such, who the real deputies were, maybe those that I think were really were the deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, please assist us as much as you can, either the ones you believe were the deputies or the people who you say portrayed themselves as deputies, tell us the names, please.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dubravko Pehar, somebody whose last name was Jakovljevic, and somebody whose last name was Peric, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And of the three, are those the only three names you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in the unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: His -- your brother's deputy commanders.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would place a bet on these three names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just in light of your answer a moment ago, are you saying that those -- these three, the three individuals who you just named, they were in fact deputies or did they fall into that category of persons you said who portrayed themselves as deputies?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you asked me whether I knew who Vinko's deputies were. I said I didn't know. Upon your insistence I am making an assumption that one of the three could be -- could have been Vinko's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how about Ernest Takac, who is indicated, described in Exhibit P633 that we were reading a few moments ago? Was Mr. Takac one of the deputy commanders?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't place my bet on him, whether he was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was your brother's superior officer? Who was the commander who gave him orders during 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it must have been somebody from the command of the town. At what level, hard to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You say assume, sir. Should the Judges understand, then that you don't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was somebody from the command of the town, but who it was who had command over Vinko's unit, who was at the level to have authority over Vinko at the time, I don't know. That is, I'm not able to give you the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us many things that your brother told you. Did he ever tell you that Tuta was one of the 15 people who had Herceg-Bosna in their hands?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what -- how am I going to help you if I'm going to give you a hearsay answer? But to make things easier for you, I shall answer and say no, he has never told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you joined HOS, you said, and how long did you remain a member of HOS?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven or eight questions ago, I answered that. I said between mid-June, 1992, until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then later, you joined the HVO and were a member of the 4th Battalion, I believe you testified yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Either I have misspoke or you have misunderstood me. I first joined the 4th Battalion and after that, I became a member of a HOS unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So when you said the 4th Battalion yesterday, you were talking about the 4th Battalion of what, what armed force?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is too much for me. I don't know. I can just tell you that there were first, the 2nd, the 3rd, the 4th, the 5th, the 6th, the 7th battalions. For simple reason these battalions were deployed around the city, in various parts of the city, and to give you any more information, I can't, because I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, you're telling this Chamber you don't know the military force that you were part of?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. I am telling this Chamber that I don't know which formation it was. I even don't know when you use the word formation, what it means. I was a member of the 4th Battalion and I apologise to the Chamber, I don't know whether I have -- I'm allowed to say that, I was a member of the battalion which was gathered in the area of Scheveningen [as interpreted] and that Scheveningen area in Mostar is called Balinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have to admit I've never heard of an area of Mostar called Scheveningen, but is there such an area, sir? Or is that a translation problem?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I explain? All the battalions in Mostar were named after the neighbourhoods where they were formed. Mostar has a neighbourhood called Rudnik, because in that area of Mostar, there used to be a mine, a coal mine. That battalion had the name Rudarska battalion. The battalion whose member I was, the 4th Battalion, was a battalion from Balinovac, and it was very easy for me to remember which battalion was which. Personally, I think, but I don't claim that, at the moment when I joined the 4th Battalion, there was no bigger formation above it. Please don't hold me to that, but I believe that we had not reached that point yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, were you in the 4th Battalion of the Serb army, of the JNA? Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me? Can you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Were you a member of the 4th Battalion of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, again, sir, do you know what part -- what army the 4th Battalion was part of? Were you issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Croatian Defence Council that the battalion belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. And approximately -- and when was it that you joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So were you a member of HOS and the HVO at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You said you were a member of HOS until the end of 1992. And you said you joined the HVO at the beginning of 1992. So are those dates not correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you doing this to confuse me or am I saying things incorrectly? You asked me twice about the HOS. I said mid-June, 1992, until the end of 1992 and now I've just told you that at the beginning of 1992, I joined the HVO, and I think that we are talking about two different periods of time. I am giving you approximate times, just like you do all the time. You are asking me about approximate periods of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'll leave the record as it is. What was your rank or position in the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was your function?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To make rounds, to patrol, to watch the front line facing the Serbs in the eastern part of Mostar, at the foot of the Velez Mountain, and the neighbouring villages, Bijelo Polje, Rastani and what not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you what we might call, maybe you didn't use this term at the time, but a private or a foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all privates or foot soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you ever at any time during your tenure of service in the HVO ever an officer?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was your commander? Who was your superior officer at the time that you served in the HVO 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not serve in the 4th Battalion -- actually it was the 4th Battalion. And the commander was Mr. Tihomir Misic, the late Timir Misic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And he was your immediate superior? There were no other commanders, company commanders, platoon leaders, he was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A platoon leader at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe his name was Veselko Cerkez. And later on, there was another person whose last name was Kopilas and I can't recall his first name, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, all the information you just gave me, was that true throughout the period of your service in the HVO? More specifically, were you always a member of the 4th Battalion? Or did you ever change units?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period between the beginning of 1992 and mid-June, 1992, is that the period you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, whatever the time period you served and only you can tell us, sir, I can't tell you, during the entire period of your service in the Croatian Defence Council military, were you always part of the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the HVO, I was a member of the 4th Battalion. My commander was the late Tihomir Misic. And the other two commanders at the lower level, platoon commanders, there may have been a third name but I doubt it. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
