utterances.text: I think the answer is perhaps no, but just so the record is very clear, your testimony is that you were never a member of your brother's unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Mrmak unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of the Mrmak or Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Chamber, please, when you were in the 4th Battalion, what locations or positions were you assigned to in Mostar? Or were you assigned to positions in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of this conflict, part of the 4th Battalion was on the old bridge, on one bank of the river was the HVO and on the other bank of the river was the Serbian army, that is the JNA. After that, I spent all the time, when I was carrying a weapon, I was in the hills on the slopes of the Mount Velez, on its southern and northern slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, just so the record is clear, if you could look again, please, if you still have it or if the usher can assist, please, on P11.18, can you tell us, sir, is there any location shown on that map or diagram where at any time during 1993 you were positioned as a member of the HVO 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are again referring to 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, sir, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I already told you that I was in the HVO from the beginning of 1992 until June, approximately, as you asked me, approximately, of that year, and then until the end of 1992, I was in a HOS unit. Why are you now asking me about 1993? In 1993, I did not participate in the war, and I did not carry a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I appreciate that clarification. So you were never in the HVO and had no military responsibilities during the entire period of 1993? Correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. If you are talking about command responsibility, military responsibility, if you are referring to war activities and participation of that kind, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I do not want to argue over words with you. Were you a member of the HVO military at any time in 1993? Whatever your function, were you a member of the HVO during calendar year 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't want to argue with you. In 1993, I was working on the calculation of war damages. War damages and all the other similar jobs were done by the HVO. If that, in your words, is membership of the HVO, then yes. This lasted for eight months, the calculation of war damages. Then the answer is yes. But if you are implying military involvement, the answer is absolutely no, and please don't ask me that same question again, because the answer is absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during the time that you were working in the HVO on war damages -- calculation of war damages, where did you perform this work? Where were you located?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building which, before the war, during the war, and to this very day, is called the building of architects. It is a huge building company that engages in the design and building of large-scale projects. During 1993, in that building, there were different offices housing different services, ranging from a small surgery to the offices which were engaged in geodetic works and my office, that I collaborated with, there was also an office that was making a list of war victims. This building is in the very centre of the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, if we could go to private session for one moment and the witness could be shown the version of P11.18 that he marked earlier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will make a break and we'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I merely wanted to ask you do the lead counsel indeed have to stay here or perhaps can I go to that meeting and leave my co-counsel and assistant behind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I'd really like to hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's entirely in your hands. You may go there and Mr. Meek can stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you a few questions for a few minutes about the 9th and 10th of May, 1993. If I understood you correctly, sir, you said that on that particular day, that is the 9th of May, you happened to be travelling back to Mostar, and when you got into the area of Mostar, you were stopped by military police unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was that an HVO military police unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to make a correction. I'm not sure whether there were military police or just plain troops, but in either of the cases, it was the HVO, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately where this checkpoint or location was where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above the town of Mostar, there was a road leading westward, leading westward, that you took to go into the town or leave it. It was perhaps four or five kilometres along that road. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you remember approximately the time of day? And certainly, sir, I'm not going to ask you to the minute, but when you arrived at this place where you were stopped by the HVO, was it -- had the light come up in the morning or what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you recall how long it was that you were held or stopped at that location?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have any understanding, sir, why it was that the HVO military unit that stopped you, let you then proceed on into Mostar, when there was fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm just asking if you had any understanding why it was, or was any statement made to you when they passed you on, as to how it was that you could go into Mostar during the fighting, by all indications was quite heavy by that time?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, I wasn't aware of how heavy was the fighting. It was the crest of the hill, and when you reach it, you can hear the fire and you can also see the town. So there was nothing unclear about it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And this police or the troops who were there said that it wasn't really particularly advisable to go into town but we did because we insisted that we be let through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you aware at that time, sir, did you become aware sometime later, that the HVO units would not let any international agencies into Mostar on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that but I do not think that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, approximately what time was it then, that you arrived at this restaurant that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that place is about four or five kilometres away from the town, a vehicle will take five to ten minutes. Well, say 30 -- 30 minutes from the time when I was stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say perhaps somewhere between 9.30 and 10.00 on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you have any trouble reaching this location? I mean, again there was fighting going on, did you just jump in your car and drive straight to the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reached the restaurant on foot, going from my flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you drove first to your flat and then you proceeded on foot to the restaurant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If I can have the usher's assistance, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. President, again to protect the markings we would have to go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you testified yesterday that on the 10th of May, the next day, -- let me -- strike that. Let me go back. Staying on the 9th of May for a moment longer, now, you've testified this afternoon, I believe, that on the 9th and 10th of May, that were you not -- is it correct that you said that you were not a member of HOS or the HVO, the military HVO at that time? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did I hear you say yesterday that when you were moving about on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, that you at some point collected your weapon? Perhaps the weapon that had been given to you when you were in one of those organisations?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So did you consider yourself, sir, on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, did you consider yourself a combatant?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the 10th of May, then, did you -- did I hear you correctly that some of the former HOS members, that had been in the Mostar HOS -- I think it was your word rallied around your brother and took up positions around Mostar? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Mostar, but at a very specific -- in a very specific area, but more or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. What specific area, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the day I managed to get near the health centre, I say near, and it was already sight-exposed to major casualties, to major danger and Vinko was in front. But whether it was to the left or to the right and how much forward, I cannot tell you but the scene is the health centre. That is, that is what they call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the correct, then, sir, the Judges can understand that as early as the 10th of May, 1993, a unit of armed men had formed themselves around your brother at the health centre on the Bulevar in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you listen to me attentively yesterday or if you read the transcript, it says and said that as we were moving towards the health centre we also came across some other groups of people, which should mean that in that area, that is what I said yesterday, there were several groups of people, which like that, believe it or not, without any particular plan, following some inertia, were moving forward. Around whom it did they rally and how strong were they, I couldn't tell you, but in any event, there were about seven or eight men around Vinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did you not testify yesterday that a group of former HOS members rallied around your brother on the 10th of May, 1993, and took up a position on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, had they taken the positions on the front line is something that I definitely did not say. So some friends, acquaintances, men, gathered around him, and for major part, they were men from HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, why did they, then -- I mean, let me understand you further: Why did these men rally around your brother?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my brother joined them, because they all knew one another. It's wartime. So I enter a coffee bar or restaurant and then I approach somebody I know, somebody I trust, not let alone war, when there is gunfire going on, I think you're asking me a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you want to change your testimony that your brother then around this time formed the unit Mrmak of which he was the commander? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not want to change my statement, and it says correctly that the unit called Mrmak was formed after a certain period of time. The circumstances and the date of its formation, I tell you once again, and believe me, I do not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, you told us I think yesterday once in these words and once the transcript, I believe, will show words to this effect, that these people rallied around your brother because he was quote "a natural leader." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, and I say so today, but please, don't ask me to recount identically word for word what I said yesterday because tomorrow I'll tell you the same thing but perhaps using a different sequence of words, but I think along those same lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say your brother was a natural leader, is it correct, sir, that men followed him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in combat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Men took direction from him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In combat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Men followed your brother's example?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess if he decided to jump off a tall building, that those others wouldn't follow in his steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, sir, that if your brother was a leader of men and if he set an example, to your knowledge, his men followed that example?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in combat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, where was the headquarters of your brother's unit located in 1993? Whether you called it the Mrmak or Vinko Skrobo, where was the headquarters of your brother's unit located?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located on Zagrebacka or Kalemova Street, the first building as you enter the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to use the map again, so if we could go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, the place that you have identified as the headquarters of your brother's unit, had you ever known that the building that that -- that housed those offices, the building that the headquarters was in, was that sometimes known or had it previously been known as Kajtaz's house? Perhaps I'm corrected by counsel, Kajtaz? K-A-J-T-A-Z?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How many times, can you tell the Judges, please, approximately how many times were you ever physically at the headquarters itself?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of times, on a few occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Two or three, not more than five times? Should we understand that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three times, not more than five, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as you've told us so far, I take it the answer to the question -- my next question is no, but you never had any duties or assignment at those headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, the location called the health centre, did I understand you correctly yesterday that you were never at that location?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean never? You mean during the war, before the war, after the war? Could you be more precise, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Fair enough. During the war in 1993, you were never at the health centre?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So is it correct, sir, that the Judges can understand that in connection with everything you've told us in the last day and a half, you were only ever at the headquarters no more -- perhaps two or three times, no more than five times in all of 1993, and you were never at the health centre? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked questions about soldiers, other soldiers, that in the midst of committing such things as expelling people from their flats or plundering flats in West Mostar, you say that some people would use your brother's name or say things like "Stela's boys." Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that the reason that people would use your brother's name and say such things as Stelici or Stela's boys because your brother and his unit were notorious for being involved in those activities?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true, and I cannot allow to you claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, why is it that of all the people of names they might have used that according to you these people just picked your brother's name? They could have said any sort of names presumably, but why would they pick your brother's name then?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps such a name, some other name that they could have used?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No. They could have said 4th Battalion boys. They could have said some other group. Why was it that you say -- if you know. If you don't know you can tell us you don't know. But why would they pick your brother's name or his unit's name?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know, sir. I know it, sir, and I -- that is something that I spoke about the whole day yesterday, and I'll do so today if need be. So in a nutshell, it was a concoction of putting false facts together, and Vinko started fighting against it too late. He began to oppose it too late, because he did not understand. He did not believe that there was a conspiracy, and why Vinko -- yesterday you had the opportunity to hear many reasons and I can repeat them today. He was a very popular person in a small town with a small unit and he did a great without any political support, without any financial support. And this is something you didn't ask me but I'll tell you. I personally had an argument with a high official of the military police who did not know that Vinko Martinovic was my brother because that person and I did not know one another, and he was sitting in a company and saying how he personally had interceded in a situation when Vinko's units or a part of it left the separation line, entered facilities, that is buildings, and looted -- and lived in them and then looted and plundered and I said to that man, "Sir that all would have been correct, but since you are not from Mostar you do not realise that in the rear of Vinko's line there is not a single building with an elevator." So I can give you the full name of this individual but I won't do it in an open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We will go to private session, then, if the President will agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And directing your attention, sir, specifically to an event that counsel directed your attention to yesterday, or perhaps this morning, or excuse me, earlier today, did you actually see personally any prisoners around your brother's area of responsibility on the 17th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, yesterday, Mr. Seric asked me if I remembered that date. Is that the date you are asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that I'm asking about the same date that Mr. Seric asked you about. So whatever that date was in your mind, on that day, did you personally -- again with your own two eyes -- see any Muslim prisoners in your brother's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I would like to tell you that I couldn't, because on that day, I was not in that area of responsibility, in the area of responsibility there was a war going on, and there was shooting going on and therefore I could not see what you are asking me if I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The time when you said you saw the lorry deliver a group of prisoners to your brother's area of responsibility, was the lorry being driven than day by someone named Dinko?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. To be honest, I don't even remember whether there was anybody in the lorry at the time or had he already gone out of the lorry. I really didn't register that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Immediately next to, and perhaps one might say part of, your brother's headquarters on Kalemova Street, there was a garage facility, was there not? Or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There was no garage immediately in the immediate area of your brother's headquarters? By that, I mean like right next to it, the next building, or any such thing as that. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the headquarters, there was a facility, a building, which was a catering facility, not a garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know if there was another garage on the other side of Kalemova Street near, again, the Ladovina restaurants that your brother or his unit used?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today, and then, there was no garage as an independent building, and I can claim that and say that for a fact because that's a -- my profession. If there wasn't then, then there isn't a garage now. Whether any of the buildings around the Ladovina contained a garage, I don't know, and I can't say either yes or no to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that Muslim prisoners from the Heliodrom, in addition to being taken to the health centre area, were also taken and used in a garage used by your brother's unit near the Vinko Skrobo headquarters?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you have just read to me is your representation. This is what you claim. But I can't confirm that. I repeat there was no garage. Maybe we don't understand each other but, again, there was no garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it also correct that Muslim prisoners from the Heliodrom were used to work at your brother's house on the locations you've marked on the Exhibit 11.18?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have the exhibit back, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We will have to go into private session, then, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the usher could please show you Exhibit P540? It should be in the bundle that was provided to everyone in the courtroom earlier. Sir, directing your attention to the -- of course, you can look at the Croatian language version -- this appears to be a report by someone named Stipe Maric dated the 27th of July, 1993, concerning the allocation of certain apartments or flats in Mostar. Now, if I direct your attention, please, if you will see the second group of names, the second list of names, you see number 15, your brother, Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to number 7? No, no, no. I can see it now. Number 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, number 15 in the second list. You see your brother's name, correct? Yes?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: By the way, before we move off that page, at least in the English version, if you look at the people to whom this document was sent, is that the same Radoslav Lavric that were you telling us about a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I don't know whether it is the same person but the first name and the last name are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, according to this document, if you look please at the text immediately above the second set of 16 names, do you agree with me, sir, that the document says, "Furthermore we would like to inform you that members of your unit are located under the following numbers" and number 15 is Vinko Martinovic. Now if we go up to number 15 in the first list, sir, isn't that indeed the Splitska address that you told us about earlier today?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the address is concerned, it is correct, Splitska, but I don't know what is the meaning of whose unit and other things, because I haven't read the document but the address is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us that some Muslims in the area of Mostar where you and your family had lived would -- had sometimes approached your brother or your family about being protected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this was in private session so if I can go to private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Mr. Scott how long are you going to take in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have finally picked up speed but let me note for the record that when it takes us 20 minutes to establish whether the witness was in the HVO in 1993, it does take sometime to cover this material. However, as I said, we have picked up speed but we will not be able to finish before 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would think, Your Honour, I will finish well within the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, definitely tomorrow, we'll hear the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No question from my mind on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I hope during the first sitting, you will leave us sometime for the cross-examination -- for the re-examination and the Judges' questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no reason to think that won't be the case. As I said, we have finally in the last half hour or so began to pick up some speed, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, -- excuse me, we may have gone past it now, but a few moments ago you said every Croat in West Mostar had his Muslim. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town of Mostar was a town of mixed population, mixed ethnic structure, a town with -- a town of mixed marriages, a town of many relations and so on and so forth. My sister's husband is a Serb by origin, and he had his family. My sister's husband could also have been a Muslim, and of course again with the family behind him. So every citizen of Mostar had a partner or partners, a number of people about whom -- after whom they looked, because it was one town. You couldn't just cut it like a Gordian knot. That is everybody looked after one or more Muslims, one or more families. Everybody asked somebody else, "Can you help he me with this, can you help me with food, can you help me get a paper or whatever" people were needing and people were needing all sorts of things at that time. That is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, at one point in your time or actually several times you said that your brother Stela had no military authority that allowed him or that would have allowed him to make any decisions concerning the treatment of Muslims. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't hold it against me. You are a Prosecutor and I am, you know, like, but what do you mean when you say "treatment"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I think that was the word that came across in the transcript. I'm not trying to trick you, but I'm trying to understand your testimony. Was it your position yesterday that your brother had no military authority that would have allowed him to take any decisions concerning how Muslims would be treated or handled in his area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this was not mentioned yesterday. There was only a question as to whether it was possible to impose discipline, and how, in one's unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, at least so far to my memory, I remember something in the line of the question put by the Prosecution. But the witness has the opportunity to agree with the Prosecution or disagree with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll have one of my colleagues try and see if they can find the place in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But sir, if I misheard you please correct me, but isn't one of the things that you wanted to tell the Judges yesterday was that why in your view your brother had no military authority in connection with the treatment of Muslims? Now, if I heard you incorrectly, just tell me so, please.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no need for us to talk in this way. So Vinko Martinovic did not have any military authority or decision-making powers, where, how, when, with Muslims. I am bothered by this maltreatment but Vinko Martinovic did not have such powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, could your brother Stela not give orders to his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you suggesting to the junction that he could not order what work would be done by the prisoners at his headquarters or at the health centre, that was not his decision as to what work they would be assigned to?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not want to say that. I believe it must have been his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You testified on one occasion, I think, that you said that your brother Stela had the ability at one point to stop HVO soldiers from firing when some people were allowed to cross the confrontation line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say he had the ability to stop, because preventing or stopping, it means some kind of repression. What I said that he could not always, but he could ensure a cease-fire, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He could ensure a cease-fire, sir, because his soldiers would follow his orders, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come, no. Some two hours ago you said you did not want to argue with me, but it seems that that is what you do want to do, but I don't want to argue with you. He was in a situation to stop the fire because on the other side of the fire line, there was a unit consisting of people who knew personally members on this side. So with shouting or, I don't know how, the fire would be stopped. So don't put it in my mouth that I said that he said, "Fire stop," and then it stops. I believe I was clear yesterday and that I'm just as clear today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said, I think, if I heard you correctly, that your brother Stela sent members of his unit packing when they did not -- when did he did something he disapproved you. Did I hear you correctly on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I hear the interpretation again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if the translators need me to repeat the question but I'll read my question to you again: You said, I think, if I heard you correctly, that your brother Stela sent members of his unit packing when they did not -- and I corrected myself -- when they did something he disapproved of.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It happened a couple of times, he'd just throw such a person from his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You also said that your brother reported -- I think your words were -- excessive behaviour. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you can assist us, what was considered excessive behaviour?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, even just the last few minutes we have actually covered a fair amount of my remaining outline and I am about to change topics and I don't believe I'll be able to complete it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry we have to keep you here another day. As I advised you yesterday, do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony today. You are still under the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understood your instructions and I complied with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 6.58 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
